INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60001, 'What is the maximum cable length for a single EtherNet/IP segment using Cat5e copper cable?', '["50 meters", "100 meters", "200 meters", "500 meters"]', 1, 'EtherNet/IP follows standard Ethernet specifications: maximum 100 meters for a single copper cable segment.', 1),
(60001, 'A ControlLogix PLC loses communication with a remote I/O rack. The switch port link light is OFF. What is the most likely cause?', '["IP address conflict", "RPI timeout too short", "Physical layer failure: cable disconnected, damaged, or switch port failure", "Firmware mismatch"]', 2, 'No link light means the physical layer connection is not established—bad cable, disconnected connector, or failed switch port.', 2),
(60001, 'What does RPI (Requested Packet Interval) control in an EtherNet/IP network?', '["The baud rate of the network", "How often the PLC requests data from a device", "The maximum number of devices on the network", "The IP address assignment method"]', 1, 'RPI defines how frequently the controller requests data from a device.', 3),
(60001, 'Which network topology provides the highest fault tolerance for industrial EtherNet/IP?', '["Star topology", "Daisy-chain topology", "Device Level Ring (DLR)", "Bus topology"]', 2, 'Device Level Ring provides redundant paths so a single cable break does not take down the network.', 4),
(60001, 'You see CRC errors incrementing on a managed switch port connected to a VFD. What is the most likely cause?', '["IP address conflict", "Electromagnetic interference from the VFD corrupting data on the cable", "Switch firmware bug", "Too many devices on the network"]', 1, 'CRC errors indicate data corruption. VFDs generate significant EMI that can couple into nearby Ethernet cables.', 5),
(60001, 'What is the purpose of IGMP snooping on an industrial Ethernet switch?', '["To prevent unauthorized access", "To limit multicast traffic to only the ports that need it", "To increase cable length limits", "To assign IP addresses automatically"]', 1, 'IGMP snooping forwards multicast traffic only to ports with interested devices instead of flooding all ports.', 6),
(60001, 'A DeviceNet network has intermittent faults. You measure 24.8V at the power tap but only 18.2V at the far end. What is the problem?', '["Normal voltage drop", "Excessive voltage drop from undersized cable or too many devices drawing power", "The power supply is failing", "A device has a shorted network connection"]', 1, 'Excessive voltage drop indicates the trunk cable may be too long, too thin, or overloaded with devices.', 7),
(60001, 'What is the key difference between implicit and explicit messaging in EtherNet/IP?', '["Implicit is faster; explicit is more reliable", "Implicit is scheduled/cyclic for real-time I/O; explicit is on-demand for configuration and diagnostics", "Implicit uses TCP; explicit uses UDP", "No difference"]', 1, 'Implicit messaging is cyclic I/O data (UDP). Explicit messaging is on-demand request/response (TCP) for configuration.', 8),
(60001, 'You need to add a device to a 192.168.1.0/24 network. Which situation would cause a conflict?', '["Using 192.168.1.254", "Using 192.168.2.1", "Using an address already assigned to another device", "Using 192.168.1.0"]', 2, 'An IP conflict occurs when two devices share the same address on the same subnet.', 9),
(60001, 'What is the recommended practice for separating industrial control network traffic from office IT traffic?', '["Use different colored cables", "Use VLANs or physically separate networks with a managed firewall between them", "Use longer cables for industrial", "No separation needed"]', 1, 'VLANs or physical separation with a firewall prevents office traffic from impacting real-time control and provides security.', 10);

INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60002, 'A 4-20mA pressure transmitter reads 12 mA. Calibrated for 0-100 PSI. What is the current pressure?', '["12 PSI", "50 PSI", "60 PSI", "75 PSI"]', 1, '4mA=0, 20mA=100. Span is 16mA. 12-4=8mA. (8/16)*100 = 50 PSI.', 1),
(60002, 'What is the primary advantage of 4-20mA over 0-10V for long cable runs?', '["Higher resolution", "Current signals are immune to voltage drop over long cable runs", "Faster response time", "Lower cost"]', 1, 'Current signals maintain accuracy regardless of cable resistance because the transmitter adjusts voltage to maintain correct current.', 2),
(60002, 'A proximity sensor has brown, blue, and black wires. What is the black wire per IEC standards?', '["Power positive", "Power negative/ground", "Signal output", "Shield"]', 2, 'Per IEC 60947-5-2: Brown=+V, Blue=0V, Black=output signal.', 3),
(60002, 'A thermocouple reads 50F low. Cold junction compensation is correct. Most likely cause?', '["Wire too long", "Thermocouple degraded from high-temperature exposure (drift)", "Transmitter miscalibrated", "Wrong TC type selected"]', 1, 'Thermocouples degrade at high temperatures as junction metallurgy changes, causing downward drift.', 4),
(60002, 'What happens to a 4-20mA transmitter output when the sensor wire breaks?', '["Goes to 0 mA", "Stays at last reading", "Goes to ~3.6 mA or 21+ mA depending on burnout configuration", "Oscillates"]', 2, 'Most transmitters drive output to a known fault state (below 4mA or above 20mA) on sensor failure.', 5),
(60002, 'An RTD (Pt100) reads 138.5 ohms. What temperature does this indicate?', '["38.5C", "100C", "138.5C", "385C"]', 1, 'Pt100: 100 ohms at 0C, +0.385 ohms/C. 138.5-100=38.5 ohms. 38.5/0.385 = 100C.', 6),
(60002, 'Why is a 3-wire RTD connection preferred over 2-wire?', '["Backup wire", "Compensates for lead wire resistance", "Increases range", "Faster response"]', 1, 'The third wire measures lead resistance so it can be subtracted from the total reading.', 7),
(60002, 'An ultrasonic level sensor reads erratically on a hot tank with steam. Why?', '["Sensor too far away", "Steam scatters the ultrasonic signal", "Liquid too viscous", "Electrical interference"]', 1, 'Steam and temperature gradients scatter ultrasonic waves. Radar sensors are preferred for these applications.', 8),
(60002, 'Correct mounting for a pressure transmitter measuring steam?', '["Above the pipe, port up", "Below the pipe with a pigtail siphon", "Same level as pipe", "Orientation does not matter"]', 1, 'For steam, mount below with pigtail siphon. Condensate in the siphon protects the diaphragm from live steam.', 9),
(60002, 'A mag meter reads 0 flow but pump is running. What should you check?', '["Pipe is empty", "Fluid conductivity too low", "Electrode coating", "All of the above"]', 3, 'All three conditions can cause a mag meter to read zero and should be checked systematically.', 10);

INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60003, 'What is the primary safety device preventing robot operation when a human enters the cell?', '["E-stop button", "Safety-rated area scanner or light curtain on the cell perimeter", "Built-in collision detection", "Warning sign"]', 1, 'Safety-rated perimeter guarding automatically stops the robot when the zone is breached.', 1),
(60003, 'A 6-axis robot has repeatability of +/-0.02mm. What does this mean?', '["Can reach any point within 0.02mm", "Returns to the same point within +/-0.02mm of average each time", "Maximum reach is 0.02mm", "Moves at 0.02mm/s"]', 1, 'Repeatability measures consistency of returning to the same taught point over many cycles.', 2),
(60003, 'What type of motion moves the TCP in a straight line between two points?', '["Joint motion (MOVJ)", "Linear motion (MOVL)", "Circular motion (MOVC)", "Free motion"]', 1, 'Linear motion interpolates the TCP along a straight line in Cartesian space.', 3),
(60003, 'Robot faults with Axis 2 Overcurrent at the same position every cycle. Most likely cause?', '["Motor failing", "Payload exceeds capacity at that reach position", "Encoder miscalibrated", "Programming error"]', 1, 'At extended reach, gravitational torque on axis 2 increases. Payload may exceed rated capacity at that position.', 4),
(60003, 'What is the purpose of robot mastering (calibration)?', '["Test motors", "Establish relationship between encoder counts and actual joint angles", "Set max speed", "Configure I/O"]', 1, 'Mastering establishes the zero-reference for each axis encoder so the robot knows its true position.', 5),
(60003, 'What limits a cobot force and speed when a human is nearby?', '["Operator reduces speed manually", "Safety-rated power/force limiting per ISO/TS 15066", "Separate safety PLC", "Standard programming limits"]', 1, 'ISO/TS 15066 defines power and force limiting requirements for collaborative robots.', 6),
(60003, 'If TCP is incorrectly defined, what symptom occurs?', '["Robot moves faster", "Robot rotates around wrong point causing incorrect paths during reorientation", "Robot faults on every move", "Robot ignores waypoints"]', 1, 'Wrong TCP means rotations pivot around the wrong point, causing tool tip deviation from intended path.', 7),
(60003, 'What is a singularity in robot kinematics?', '["Maximum speed point", "Configuration where axes align causing infinite solutions and potentially violent motion", "Maximum payload point", "Software error"]', 1, 'At singularity, inverse kinematics has infinite solutions, causing extreme axis speeds to maintain TCP path.', 8),
(60003, 'After a collision, axis 3 shows 2.5 degree position error. What must be done?', '["Jog to home and restart", "Re-master the axis, verify TCP, run program at reduced speed", "Replace axis 3 motor", "Ignore it"]', 1, 'Collision can shift mechanical zero. Re-mastering and TCP verification are required before resuming.', 9),
(60003, 'Difference between work envelope and interference zone?', '["Same thing", "Work envelope is total reachable space; interference zone is where path overlaps with other equipment or human access", "Work envelope for robot; interference for humans", "Interference always larger"]', 1, 'Work envelope is total reachable space. Interference zone is the subset where conflicts with other equipment or humans can occur.', 10);
